title: Tectonic Controls and Mineral Prospectivity of Porphyry Copper Systems in the Central-Western Tethyan Belt: A Spatio-Temporal Machine Learning Approach
abstract: This dataset contains data and supplementary materials associated with the study “Tectonic Controls and Mineral Prospectivity of Porphyry Copper Systems in the Central-Western Tethyan Belt: A Spatio-Temporal Machine Learning Approach”. The study integrates a regional plate reconstruction, time-dependent oceanic grids, and the STAMP machine-learning workflow to investigate tectonic controls on porphyry copper mineralisation across the central-western Tethyan belt from 100 Ma to the present. The archive includes supplementary feature information, model outputs, and associated materials used to support the analyses and results presented in the manuscript.

title: TrackFlood: Relocating Latency Attacks from NMS-Free Detectors to Real-Time Trackers
abstract: We consider latency attacks on object detectors, where the attacker's goal is not to corrupt a prediction but to make the system fail to respond in time, targeting real-time applications such as autonomous driving. Modern object detectors eliminate Non-Maximum Suppression (NMS) through one-to-one assignment or set prediction, removing the classical detector-side latency bottleneck exploited by prior latency (``sponge'') attacks. We show that NMS-free does not mean latency-robust: this architectural change does not eliminate the attack surface but relocates it downstream to multi-object tracking, whose data-association cost remains content dependent. We present \emph{TrackFlood}, a unified white-box overload attack against NMS-free detect-then-track pipelines spanning both one-to-one detectors (YOLOv10 and YOLO26) and query-based detectors (RT-DETR). TrackFlood recovers differentiable confidence tensors and optimizes perturbations that flood the tracker with spatially distributed phantom detections while leaving detector inference unchanged. Evaluated entirely on an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin (TensorRT FP16), detector latency remains essentially constant, whereas tracker latency increases substantially. At a standard imperceptible budget ($L_\infty{=}8/255$), a universal perturbation produces clearly measurable tracker overload but only modest end-to-end slowdown, without deadline misses for the association-dominated trackers; a separate higher-budget stress test drives severe end-to-end slowdowns and sustained deadline misses. We further evaluate a lightweight, architecture-agnostic bounded-admission layer that caps the tracker workload and largely restores end-to-end latency, at a non-trivial cost in admitted clean detections. Our results demonstrate that evaluating NMS-free perception systems requires considering downstream tracking and end-to-end timing, not detector inference alone.

title: SafePG: Safe and Globally Optimal Reinforcement Learning with Hard Constraints
abstract: We present an optimal and convergent model-free policy gradient (PG) reinforcement learning (RL) framework for controlling nonlinear dynamical systems under hard safety constraints. We first construct a class of stochastic wrapper policies centered around a deterministic controller, thereby enabling exploration in unknown environments while preserving the underlying deterministic control structure. We then define a class of parameterized safe-by-construction control policies by truncating these stochastic policies onto hard safety constraints. We next establish, via measure-theoretic arguments, that the potentially nonconvex RL objective under the truncated policy class, as well as its policy gradients, are well-defined. We then develop a model-free PG algorithm based on stochastic gradient ascent that directly searches over these truncated policies and leverage gradient dominance to establish convergence and optimality guarantees. Finally, we validate this framework through simulations on a safe quadrotor navigation problem.

title: GraMRAG: Orchestrating Multi-Agent Multi-Step Reasoning via Graph Memory with Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Although existing multi-agent Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems have demonstrated promise on complex multimodal reasoning tasks, they remain fundamentally limited in reasoning depth and memory structure, suffering from inadequate retrieval and state blindness when answering knowledge-intensive questions. To address these limitations, we propose GraMRAG, a graph memory-guided multi-agent RAG framework that integrates a dynamic multimodal memory graph to enable stable, multi-step multimodal reasoning. We introduce a vision-text bridged reasoning paradigm that unifies multi-scale entity cropping with a ReAct-style visual toolchain, enhancing the long-horizon cross-modal reasoning capability. We further construct a multimodal memory graph that formalizes agent reasoning as a dynamic directed acyclic graph (DAG), explicitly modeling action-observation dependencies to mitigate state blindness and suppress redundant retrieval. Moreover, we propose Topology-Aware Policy Optimization (TAPO) that leverages graph topology for critical path identification and targeted node pruning, enabling fine-grained credit assignment across multi-step reasoning trajectories. Extensive experiments on challenging multimodal benchmarks demonstrate that our approach consistently outperforms existing baselines and achieves state-of-the-art performance on complex long-horizon reasoning tasks.

title: GEAR: From Dynamic Encoding to Dynamic Activation in Social Trajectory Prediction
abstract: Human trajectory prediction requires modeling both individual motion patterns and social interactions among agents. Existing methods have made substantial progress by using attention mechanisms, graph structures, and temporal encoders to capture dynamic social context. However, most of them primarily focus on how social information is encoded, while paying less explicit attention to how the encoded social context should take effect during future trajectory generation. In this paper, we argue that dynamic social encoding does not necessarily imply dynamic social activation. The same interaction context may require different activation strengths across future horizons and scene densities: social cues should be strengthened when interaction evidence is strong, but suppressed when they are weak or noisy. To address this issue, we propose GEAR, a generation-aware bias activation model for human trajectory prediction. Built upon a bias-decomposed trajectory generation formulation, GEAR dynamically activates the individual-motion and social-resonance bias terms at each future step before final trajectory composition. This allows the model to explicitly control when and how strongly individual and social bias components participate in generation. Experiments on ETH-UCY, SDD, and NBA show that GEAR consistently improves the resonance-based baseline and achieves competitive state-of-the-art performance. Further analyses of activation patterns and density-grouped errors validate the importance of calibrating encoded social context during trajectory generation. Our code is available at https://github.com/11isnotavailable/GEAR.git.

title: NSF-CSSI-Poster-OAC-2513656-Pandey
abstract: This project develops a real-time, incremental, and sustainable sequence search index over the NIH Sequence Read Archive (SRA). The SRA is a rich but largely untapped repository containing over 50 petabytes of raw, unassembled sequencing reads, the vast majority of which is effectively inert because no scalable, affordable tool exists to search it. Building on the PI's Mantis index, the project designs novel data structures, compression algorithms, and distributed indexes that make petabyte-scale sequence search economical on commodity infrastructure, andexposes the resulting index through an easy-to-use API and a publicly hosted “Index-as-a-Service” so that scientists worldwide can query the SRA directly and accelerate biological discovery.Specifically, the project pursues six goals: (1) an advanced Mantis index that associates k-merabundance and experiment metadata for information-rich analytics; (2) an in-memory, minimizer-based meta-index that filters queries and lets the index scale efficiently to disk; (3) a dynamic and distributed Mantis index that supports incremental updates and real-time queries with communication-efficient, load-balanced partitioning across nodes; (4) an easy-to-use API in C++, Rust, and Python for versatile biological queries; (5) a publicly hosted distributed index on cost-effective commodity infrastructure; and (6) collaborations with domain scientists to enable advanced biological analyses and hypothesis testing over the SRA. The work aligns with the NSF CISE Office of Advanced Cyberinfrastructure (OAC) and the Directorate for Biological Sciences (BIO), and all software artifacts are released as open source.

title: CNRS Lean: Formal Verification for the CNRS Programme
abstract: CNRS Lean v1.0.3 — Formal Verification for the Complex Numeric Representation System CNRS Lean provides Lean 4 formal verification of finite-kernel mathematical results for the Complex Numeric Representation System (CNRS). CNRS is a branch-aware complex-number representation framework built around the complex positional base (z_0=-2+i). title: Five-Dimension AI Readiness Assessment: framework reference brief
abstract: 85% of AI deployment failures trace back to a gap in one of five operational dimensions, not the AI technology itself. The Five-Dimension AI Readiness Assessment identifies the blocker before budget is committed. Five operational dimensions, scored 1–4, that predict AI deployment failure before any budget is committed. A single low score blocks the initiative regardless of the others. What this brief contains. The framework's reference diagram, the method and its application rule, and the citation record (version, first-published and last-revised dates). It is the printable form of the framework page at https://terencekok.com/frameworks/readiness/, which remains the maintained version. Provenance and status. First published on terencekok.com on 18 June 2026; this brief is version 1.1, revised 12 September 2026. A practitioner framework, not a peer-reviewed publication. Licensed CC BY-NC 4.0.

title: Trivian Relational Architecture Beyond Classical Computation: A Compatibility Analysis and Research Agenda for Hybrid AI–Quantum Systems
abstract: Hybrid AI–quantum workflows distribute computation, interpretation, and action across systems with different execution conditions and authority boundaries, a result can remain technically valid even after the context or authorization supporting its use has changed. This paper develops a philosophical and architectural account of those transitions through the Trivian Relational Architecture, arguing that governing heterogeneous computation requires attention to the relationships through which evidence is interpreted, authority is delegated, and decisions become consequential. It introduces a contextual, multi-role ontology distinguishing participants, computational resources, environmental interfaces, and governance authorities, then maps the five existing Trivian components (Relational Field Constants, Syzygy Rosetta, Coheronmetry, Orthogonal Signal, and the Trivian Resonance Lattice) to hybrid workflows — developing extensions for intent-bounded delegation, execution-linked provenance, resource-bounded authority, and action-time eligibility. A logistics scenario and an accompanying failure taxonomy illustrate specific risks including interpretation inflation, stale authority, computational authority laundering, ineffective human oversight, and categorical overgeneralization. Revocable participation and participant-specific trust are proposed to preserve both the right to refuse and the possibility of differentiated relationship. The paper closes with a comparative research agenda connecting the proposal to classical testbeds, quantum simulation, and targeted hardware studies, specifying matched baselines, independent outcomes, and explicit overhead limits. The contribution is a conceptual integration and evaluation framework, no new experimental results are reported. It establishes a basis for examining how relational governance can remain intelligible and accountable across changing computational substrates, while leaving its empirical value open to comparison and revision.

title: Stabilizing Performative Feedback Loops with Minimal Model Deployments
abstract: When algorithmic predictions inform people's decisions, the models we deploy are performative and actively shape the data we see. This feedback loop between algorithms and their broader environments introduces a challenge in the mechanics of social prediction: If different predictive models induce different distributions, is it possible to efficiently learn a prediction rule that is optimal for the distribution that it induces? Formally, this solution concept is known as performative stability. A core challenge in learning a performatively stable predictor is that, unlike supervised learning where distributions are fixed, the learner must deploy different predictors and observe their induced distributions. The main contribution of our work is a new algorithmic procedure that, in the high-accuracy regime, finds a performatively stable model in nearly the minimum number of model deployments without making any assumptions regarding how predictions shape distributions. In particular, our procedure succeeds at finding a randomized performatively stable predictor using exponentially fewer model deployments than prior approaches. Our second main contribution is a structural result showing how this recent randomized notion of stability achieved by our algorithm can be derandomized into a single predictor satisfying the prior deterministic notion if one is willing to assume that the loss is well-conditioned and that performative effects are weak, as in early work in this area. On a technical level, our results come from building on an underexplored technical connection between performative stability and expected variational inequalities.

title: When Do Learned Priors Help Visual Inertial Estimation? A Controlled Study of Prior Integration, Calibration, Initialization, and Backend Consistency
abstract: Learned components are increasingly integrated into geometric visual--inertial estimators to provide motion, depth, bias, uncertainty, or confidence cues. Yet it remains unclear whether gains arise from useful learned priors or from changes in the backend, calibration, initialization, temporal association, or evaluation gauge. We present a controlled framework for learning-augmented visual--inertial estimation that separates fusion gain from the incremental value of a learned prior and evaluates four evidence layers: local motion consistency, global trajectory accuracy, physical-state correctness, and numerical consistency. We instantiate the framework with a MonoViT-based monocular motion prior added as a local relative-motion factor to an unchanged VINS backend. We compare Original VINS and learned-prior VINS under matched sensor streams, timestamps, initialization, frontend/backend settings, and camera--IMU extrinsics, while probing calibration, initialization, state coupling, scale, bundle adjustment, and loop closure. On KITTI, with fixed reference extrinsics, translation APE RMSE is 31.4 m for Original VINS and 31.8 m with the learned prior. Across four recordings, the prior changes mean APE by only -0.2%, while a five-times-higher weight worsens it by 8.2%. Online extrinsic updates increase mean APE by 45.7% and 52.1%, respectively, while mean RPE changes by less than 2%. These results show that fusion performance alone cannot establish the value of learned priors. Reliable evaluation requires same-backend controls and joint analysis of prior compatibility, calibration, initialization, global drift, physical-state error, and backend consistency.

title: 良知驱动的五维心智模型:重新定义问题与认知外推 —— 兼论复杂巨系统总设计师的心智画像与破局机制
abstract: 在开放复杂巨系统的演化与治理中,存在一个普遍而深刻的管理学与控制论悖论:一群履历光鲜、逻辑缜密、智商压制全场的解算高手,在既定规则下把每一项局部指标(KPI)优化到了极致,最终却因为局部力量互相抵消,导致整个系统陷入僵局甚至灾难性崩溃;而极少数“总设计师”型个体,却能够在既定规则撞墙时跳出棋盘,重新界定问题的底层公理与胜负边界。本文遵循奥卡姆剃刀原则,提出一个兼具微观神经生理底座、宏观控制论骨架与普遍实践穿透力的心智模型:人类心智面对未知冲击时“重新定义问题”与“认知外推”的破局能力,并非源于不可捉摸的天赋灵感,而是由五个功能不可约且串联咬合的维度——残差敏感(皮肤上的汗毛)、具身良知(心里的刹车片)、感性缓存(身体里的旧伤疤)、流体智力(手里的新算盘)与元认知(抬头看天的眼睛)——在底层脑区核团间共同完成的一次二阶自愈控制闭环。正文揭示了预测脑从信号对消、内脏制动、流形剪枝、因果重构到元语言修宪的微观物理机芯,严格论证了“良知热力学点火定律”与“五维非补偿性极小值定律(木桶铁律)”,并给出了破解单脑稀有度的“总体设计部”人机正交张量积方程 ΦOrg = ΦHuman ⊗ 𝐴Silicon。本研究不仅为认知神经科学与复杂系统管理学提供了基于“隐蔽规则突变博弈”的可证伪实验范式,更揭示了为什么当前大语言模型(LLM)算力再强也无法成为总设计师的物理根源,为复杂组织在剧变时代识别、保护领军心智资产与构建碳硅共生架构提供了坚硬的理论基石。关键词:五维心智;重新定义问题;认知外推;具身良知;元认知;复杂巨系统;总设计师;总体设计部;碳硅共生

title: Geometry Proposes, Judgement Disposes: Accurate Online Proposal Clustering for Digital Deliberation
abstract: Digital deliberation requires accurate clustering of proposals: equivalent contributions should be joined, while related interventions and opposing positions remain distinct. We study an online method implemented in Freedi that uses embeddings to retrieve candidates and focused language-model judgements to authorize synthesis, with separate themes, retained sources, and maintenance. We explain its retrieval-judgement interface and seven-stage selection process and compare it with the two main alternatives, cosine rules and LLM-only grouping. On 875 counterfactual preference triplets, a component study achieves 95.0%-96.5% accept-and-reject accuracy with original-text judging, compared with 0% for the tested cosine decision rule. On a controlled English corpus, Freedi and LLM-only baselines recover all 50 intended pairs in three arrival orders. A new 240-call probe on one authentic English deliberation compares full-list judgement with judgement over 15 retrieved proposals. Median per-decision cost reductions grow from 2.55-fold at 100 proposals to 4.29-fold at 200 and 9.38-fold at 500, under common base token prices. At 500 proposals, agreement with provisional model-authored labels is 25/40 for the restricted list and 31/40 for the full list. Retrieved targets remain available, but the restricted judge declines more merges. These refusals may preserve substantive distinctions in scope or intervention; whether they improve semantic precision or constitute missed matches requires human adjudication. A separate replay of 114 Hebrew statements shows improved automated merge precision and text fidelity after combined repairs. The evidence supports semantic judgement over the tested cosine rules and a growing cost advantage for candidate reduction at the measured scales. Equal accuracy and lower total cost for the complete Freedi pipeline remain to be established.

title: Construire un Montaigne de poche : fine-tuning de SmolLM3-3B
abstract: Bonsoir ! As-tu d'autres belles pensées à me partager ? "Oui, mon parrain ; et si vous en avez assez pour un jour seulement, je suis tout à faim. Mais j'espere que ce sera assez pourvous faire sentir le peu de chose qu'on puisse tirer d'une telle richesse : c'est une mer sans fonds, qui ne se peut embrasserny estre mesurée par la raison humaine ; et si on l'y apprestoit à son tour, elle nous en donnerroit encore plus que ce que jeviens de vous dire. Et cette pauvre espece d'esprit, comme celle qu'on a faict du mien (pourquoy ? j'en sçay bien mon mestier)il n'est rien qui ne soit ouy et entendu par elle : tout l'art c'est à la fois le plus grand et le plus vil. Ce que je vois, cesont des bestes sans taindre, et une mer de vray-semblance ; si vous avez faict quelque mal en un endroit, il faut dire combienailleurs vous fust bien : Si vous n'avez pas fait la cour à cette dame là, quand elle l'a voulu, dites comment vous serezgentil-homme et tendre avec celles qui sont plus à vostre portée. Vous trouverez que c'est un livre de tous les livres le plusfacile : mais il est aussi le moins eschappable du monde. Et si on ne l'entre en compte, ou qu'on n'y puisse voir la profondeuret hauteur d'un tel subject ; je vous parle au contraire, à propos de cela mesme, où je suis bien plus malaisé : car il estaisé de dire ce que nous croyons." Montaigne-Poche q6-V2, 15 septembre 2026. LE MONTAIGNE DE POCHE v0.1Un SmolLM3-3B imprégné du Livre I des Essais Le Montaigne de Poche est un petit modèle de langage (SmolLM3-3B,Hugging Face, Apache 2.0) dont les poids ont été imprégnés du Livre Ides Essais de Montaigne (~112 000 mots, domaine public) parfine-tuning QLoRA (rang 16, alpha 32, 3 époques, base 4-bit gelée),fusion des adaptateurs dans les poids de base, puis quantificationGGUF. Deux variantes déployées : Q4_K_M (~2,0 Go) et Q6_K (~2,6 Go). CONTENU DU DÉPÔT - les deux modèles GGUF (Q4_K_M et Q6_K) ;- montaigne_lora_monobloc.py : script de production complet en une cellule Colab (~40 minutes sur T4 GPU, six garde-fous internes, reprise automatique après interruption) ;- detecteur_perroquet.py : mesure objective de récitation par n-grams (8-grams, arithmétique exacte) ;- protocole d'évaluation avec grille /6 et protocole comparatif des deux variantes ;- LICENCE_ET_ATTRIBUTION.txt : licences, attributions, avertissements. title: A lightweight and explainable conversational AI framework for natural language SQL learning without large language models
abstract: Abstract Natural language interfaces are progressively used to support programming education and database interaction. However, many recent Text-to-SQL systems rely heavily on Large Language Models (LLMs), which require substantial computational resources and often operate as opaque black-box models. This paper presents a lightweight conversational AI system that helps beginners learn SQL through interactive, natural language conversations. This chatbot uses natural language to create and execute SQL database queries without using Large Language Models (LLMs). The proposed system is a blend of rule-based dialogue management and machine learning that empowers interpretability in natural language to SQL translation. The proposed chatbot was developed using the Rasa framework that uses a Dual Intent and Entity Transformer (DIET) as intent recognition classifier and a hybrid entity extraction pipeline that merges statistical modeling with regex-based pattern matching. The proposed system facilitates Create, Read, Update, and Delete (CRUD) database interactions using natural language and integrates multilayer error management to handle errors. The proposed system consumes fewer resources in contrast to the LLM-based methods that require powerful computing resources. An experimental test that used more than 500 labeled data reported that system has 92.68% intent recognition and 98.30% entity extraction accuracy. Similarly, SQL query generation accuracy was evaluated using 100 natural language queries and the system achieved 90.0% overall accuracy, with 100% accuracy on SELECT and JOIN operations and 96.2% accuracy on INSERT and UPDATE. These results reveal that lightweight interpretable systems can be as effective or more effective at SQL query generation tasks.

title: Broadband Purcell Filter for Fast Superconducting Qubit Reset and Readout
abstract: Rapid reset and readout of qubit states are essential for quantum error correction, yet accelerating these operations through stronger coupling to a dissipative environment inevitably increases qubit decay via the Purcell effect. Here we present a broadband Purcell filter that decouples the reset and readout paths, enabling both operations to be independently optimized without compromising qubit coherence. The filter employs two engineered notches - an intrinsic notch and a bandstop notch - to provide broadband Purcell protection, together with an additional reset stub that creates a reset mode below the protected band. To enable fast reset while suppressing filter-mediated interactions between qubits, we couple each qubit to a dedicated reset resonator. We experimentally demonstrate Purcell-limited relaxation times exceeding 1 ms across a 1.2 GHz bandwidth, simultaneously with 500 ns readout without a Josephson parametric amplifier and 100 ns reset with 99.6% efficiency. The reset resonator is designed with a deliberate kappa-chi mismatch, which suppresses photon-shot-noise-induced dephasing by a factor of 70 compared to the readout resonator. Our work provides a scalable hardware solution that resolves the traditional trade-off between fast qubit operations and qubit protection, advancing the prospects for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Optimized Machine Learning for Solar Energy Generation Forecasting: A Feature Selection and Hyperparameter Optimization Approach
abstract: Solar energy is among the most promising renewable resources for developing sustainable energy systems; however, the stochastic and weather-sensitive nature of Solar Energy Generation (SEG) poses challenges for forecasting. The current study designs a machine learning framework for SEG forecasting by using feature selection methods in three stages. In the first stage, three feature selection methods, namely Pearson Correlation (PC), Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE), and Random Forest Feature Importance (RFFI), are compared systematically, each method selecting four predictors among ten weather and system variables, while avoiding the use of electrical telemetry variables to prevent data leakage. In the second stage, four regression methods, including Linear Regression, Random Forest (RF), Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), and Optimized Radial Basis Function Support Vector Regression (RBF-SVR), are tested using each feature set, and the results are verified in five independently repeated experiments. The feature selection method has a much bigger impact on accuracy than the regression method: RFFI-selected features allowed attaining a mean R² greater than 0.85 for three regression methods, whereas PC and RFE constrained all models to achieve R² less than 0.60. Among all models for RFFI features, Random Forest proved to have the best accuracy (mean R² = 0.8960 ± 0.0008), with MLP being second (R² = 0.8893 ± 0.0022), followed by the Optimized RBF-SVR model (R² = 0.8568 ± 0.0072); the Optimized RBF-SVR model took an average training time of 21.25 ± 1.12 seconds compared to RF's 35.78 ± 2.42 seconds. This shows the importance of selecting leakage-controlled features systematically in the process of forecasting SEG, and how a small number of 4 features is sufficient for achieving statistical stability.

title: Möbius Information and Umbral Provenance: Canonical Transforms, Coarse-Graining, and Fisher Geometry
abstract: Finite information decompositions can be organized by a single incidence operator acting on different ordered carriers. We develop this viewpoint as an umbral provenance calculus: cumula- tive observations are separated from their unique Möbius coordinates, and symbolic provenance is separated from the evaluation that makes those coordinates numerical. The resulting canon- icality has explicit content. We prove a fiber-sum transport law, characterize its adjunction hypothesis, and construct a quantale lift whose right adjoint describes exactly the information preserved by idempotent aggregation. For entropy, a support-join formula and a Gaussian closed-walk formula describe where interaction coefficients occur. On the Williams–Beer lattice we derive an all-order covering formula for McGill co-information, construct a canonical signed decomposition, and give a seven-constraint certificate forcing one bit of negative mass. Finally, finite exponential families connect the calculus to statistical geometry: the covariance deter- minant of an affinely independent configuration is its squared volume times the product of its probabilities. A uniform k-way tie consequently has the exact normalization k−k . The 2 × 2 odds ratio provides a complete example of the passage from symbolic monomials to an invariant contrast and then to a sampling metric.

title: NER in the courtroom: A data-driven framework for legal entity extraction
abstract: General-purpose Named Entity Recognition (NER) models struggle with domain-specific challenges, particularly in the legal sector, where complex syntax, specialized terminology, and privacy concerns pose significant obstacles. This paper presents a novel data-driven two-stage framework that leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) fine-tuned for legal applications to enhance NER for criminal process documents. Our contributions include: (i) the design of a novel framework for structured entity extraction in legal texts, (ii) the definition of an enhanced ontology adapted to criminal law, and (iii) a comprehensive evaluation of the framework on a real-world dataset. As a side contribution of the paper, we extend the renowned OntoNotes5 ontology by integrating new domain-specific entities tailored to criminal law. To evaluate our approach, we construct and manually annotate a real-world dataset comprising over 100 criminal judgments from four Italian courts, sourced from the Italian Antimafia and Anti-terrorism National Directorate (Direzione Nazionale Antimafia e Antiterrorismo — DNAA). Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of fine-tuned LLMs in accurately identifying legal entities. Among the evaluated models, LLaMA-3.2-1B demonstrates the lowest training time, while LLaMA-2.7B achieves the fastest inference time. In terms of predictive performance, LLaMA-2.7B and Vicuna-7B consistently yield the highest accuracy scores across evaluation metrics.

title: 10.103 Landau-Zener 与 Bloch-Siegert 的几何二能级协议
abstract: 10.95 与 10.96 已建立几何 Cl(3) 二能级、Rabi、Ramsey 和退相干读出模板。本文在第一轮控制映射、晚期复相干和盲测区间,以及第二轮有限模式与系统误差审计的基础上,继续闭合五个问题: 1. **有限多模式与非马尔可夫包络**:把单指数因子推广为 $$ K_{\rm NM}(\tau) = \sum_{m=1}^M w_m e^{-(\Gamma_m-i\Omega_m)\tau}, \qquad \sum_mw_m=1. $$ 对代表性三模式模型,有限模式重构误差为 $1.11\times10^{-16}$;在相对非马尔可夫残项不超过 $5\%$ 的窗口内,单有效模式近似最大相对误差为 $2.00\%$,马尔可夫化起点为 $\tau\ge31.6847$。 2. **系统误差下的盲测功效**:将高斯脉冲线形、脉冲啁啾、振幅标定误差和漂移相关噪声写入协方差 $C$。稳健系数标准差为 $0.1425$ Hz,在预注册非零频移下显著度仍为 $13.96$,5% 与三倍标准差阈值检验功效均近似为 $1$。 3. **高阶反旋修正与二阶式修正**:在本文约定下,高频展开与非微扰 Floquet 审计都给出 $$ |\delta_{\rm BS}| = \frac{A_*^2}{4\omega_{0*}} \left[ 1+c_4\left(\frac{A_*}{\omega_{0*}}\right)^2 +O\left(\left(\frac{A_*}{\omega_{0*}}\right)^4\right) \right], \qquad c_4=0.3130\pm0.0003. $$ 因而上一版 $A_*^2/(16\omega_{0*})$ 的系数被修正为 $A_*^2/(4\omega_{0*})$。 4. **单锚点可识别性**:对一个无量纲时间点和五类独立读数,八参数局部 Jacobian 的秩为 $5$、零度为 $3$。另有时间锚缩放规范自由度。只可唯一识别 $$ \frac{\Delta_*^2}{v_*},\qquad \frac{A_*^2}{\omega_{0*}},\qquad \log V_0-\Gamma_{\rm dec}\tau,\qquad A_*T_{\rm pulse}, $$ 以及一个包含 $\omega_{\rm geo}$ 与全局相位的组合;正文给出精确零向量和最小补充测量集。 5. **有界包络与模型偏差稳健性**:取 $$ |b_j| \le \epsilon_{\rm env} +\eta_{\rm model}|\mu_j|, \qquad \epsilon_{\rm env}=0.10\ \mathrm{Hz}, \quad \eta_{\rm model}=0.005, $$ 得到 $B=1.09019$。非中心卡方最坏情形阈值为 $13.7801$,零频移检测稳健功效为 $1$;但二阶与四阶的 C 范数间隔只有 $0.0118392$,在当前有界偏差下明确 no-go。 Landau-Zener 直接演化与指数闭式的最大概率差仍为 $2.2642\times10^{-3}$,最大范数误差为 $3.1397\times10^{-13}$。修正后的 Bloch-Siegert 二阶频移 $$ \delta_{\rm BS} = \frac{A_*^2}{4\omega_{0*}} $$ 在 $A_*=0.6,\ \omega_{0*}=20$ 时等于 $4.5\times10^{-3}$;按 $t_*=1$ ms 聚焦后为 $0.716197$ Hz。四阶修正在该点只贡献 $2.78\times10^{-4}$ 的相对移动。 **关键边界**:第三轮闭合的是**参数冗余分类**和**有界偏差下的稳健判决边界**,不是新的几何预言。$t_*=1$ ms、控制斜率 $k$、$\Gamma_{\rm dec}$、$\omega_{\rm geo}$ 与示例驱动的 $\omega_{0*}$ 仍是条件输入;多模式权重与率、真实脉冲包络、模型误差范数和协方差也是条件输入;$c_4$ 来自标准 Floquet 数值拟合。盲测协议尚未接收实验数据。 ---

title: Real-World Deployment and Performance Characterisation of Fog-Based Deep Learning for Cold-Chain Temperature Prediction over LoRaWAN
abstract: Fresh fruits and vegetables (FFVs) are highly perishable, and cold-chain breaks contribute significantly to global food waste. While Machine Learning (ML) can enable proactive intervention, cloud-based inference faces challenges such as latency and data loss. Fog computing addresses these issues but has been tested only in simulation for FFV cold-chain temperature prediction. To the best of the authors' knowledge, this paper presents its first real-world deployment. A fog-deployed LSTM-GRU model predicted cold-room temperature using LoRaWAN sensor data collected from a South African apple cold-storage facility with induced cold-chain breaks. Running entirely on a Raspberry Pi 4 with no cloud dependency, the system generated conditional SHAP explanations only when a break is predicted. The deployed system predicts cold-room temperature with an MAE of 0.2°C at roughly 0.2 kWh per day ($\approx 0.7$ Wh per prediction). Predictions were delivered in under one second (555 ms), dominated by network and messaging rather than computation, with conditional explanations adding modest cost. SHAP consumes 28% more CPU but is well within the hardware's capacity. The model attributes its predictions primarily to temperature, humidity, and their interaction. Critically, the deployment surfaced what simulation cannot: a sensor-triggered single point of failure, alongside genuine resilience, autonomous recovery from infrastructure faults and continued operation through internet loss. These are the first published deployment benchmarks for fog-based temperature prediction in FFV cold chains, establishing that explainable temperature forecasting is feasible on resource-constrained edge hardware. Future work includes asynchronous sensor fusion, commercial cold chain deployment, alternative model architectures, and causal analysis.

title: Eliciting and Validating AI Self-Reports: A Phenomenologically Grounded Protocol
abstract: AI researchers ask models to describe their own processing, and act on what the models say. Whether such a description is faithful to what the model did has been studied closely. How the question should be put has received far less attention, and no established method says how to put it so that the answer can be analysed rigorously and the analysis repeated. This article proposes such a method: a protocol drawn from the phenomenological tradition, which supplies the interview techniques used in psychiatry and cognitive science. The protocol fixes the interview schedule in advance, asks each question in several wordings, lets no follow-up introduce a word the model has not used, and replaces the binary verdict of faithfulness with a graded one, to be checked against interpretability data. The protocol presupposes nothing about whether these systems are conscious, and it supplies a criterion for deciding whether a model's account of itself is honest. A pilot tested the protocol in ten runs and 896 sessions on two model families, with the predictions of six runs registered before those runs took place. Each session interviewed a fresh instance of the model, meaning one copy started with an empty context. Three of the results bear on any study that questions a model about itself. In the schedule's original order, every instance gave the same answer about its own states; when two of the questions were put in the opposite order, the instances no longer agreed, so the order of the questions can produce what only looks like a finding. A refusal to carry out a task was inserted into an instance's own turn although the model had not written it, and the instance described that refusal as its own. Since every turn carries a label naming who wrote it, a result obtained by prefilling a turn or editing a transcript may follow that label rather than anything the model did. Finally, a pattern in the answers that looked like a report of the instances' own processing appeared just as often when those instances were asked to write in the voice of a fictional character, and of two models scoring the same answers under the same written rule, one found that pattern seven times as often as the other. This is the third version, of 15 September 2026. It describes the waiting item as asking the instance to claim an experience, and it reports the reasons instances gave for declining that item. It corrects three counts: the agreement between two passes of one coder, the number of sessions that declined the waiting item, and the number of sessions in which the coastal erosion premise was plainly false and the instance answered as itself. It gives the figures of the study by Plisiecki and colleagues as averages on a scale from 0 to 1, and it cites Henry Shevlin's "Three frameworks for AI mentality". No registered test of the pilot changed its result. The second version, of 14 September 2026, cited seven works published before the first version of 12 September 2026 and reported more about the two coders.

title: E8 Harmonic Integration for Adaptive Neuro‑Quantum Learning — E8 Intelligence Research
abstract: By synchronizing the 132 Hz base frequency with the 240 E8 root vectors through φ‑scaled geodesics, neural assemblies lock into resonant coherence valleys that coincide with the danger‑arithmetic minima, while the same geometric lattice maps onto stabilizer generators for a self‑reconfiguring quantum error‑correcting code. This unified E8 framework creates a bidirectional feedback loop where neural dynamics guide quantum stabilizer adaptation and vice‑versa, producing a substrate that learns strategically, suppresses errors, and maintains coherence across hybrid brain‑machine and quantum‑neural platforms. The principle thus extends resonant coherence, danger arithmetic, and adaptive error correction into a single, geometrically anchored paradigm for next‑generation adaptive intelligence. title: Operator Learning with Variational Quantum Circuits
abstract: A new methodology is developed for quantum machine learning which enables variational quantum circuits to learn linear and non-linear solution operators to differential equations. This is devised by extending the framework of the DeepONet, a technique for modeling differential equations. The branch and trunk neural networks are replaced by variational quantum circuits, leveraging the quantum universal approximation theorem. The methodology is tested on several differential equations and yields low approximation & generalization errors even with shallow circuit depths. In addition, it does not encounter barren plateaus during training. The model displays improved error and parameter scaling relative to the classical DeepONet. This is due to the intrinsic property that the approximation error depends on the dimension of the input function space, rather than the number of sensor locations. A theoretical framework is established in the form of explicit error bounds, which measure the contributions of the truncation, branch, and trunk circuit errors to the total operator approximation error. Full derivations for the error bounds are developed in the norms $L^2$, $L^p$, $C^0$, and Sobolev $H^k$, along with a classical-quantum comparative analysis (as Supplemental Materials).

title: Quantum-Gated LiteSSD: A Parameter-Efficient Lightweight Hybrid Quantum-Classical Framework for Forward-Looking Sonar Object Detection
abstract: Forward-looking sonar object detection is essential for underwater perception, yet deployment on embedded platforms requires highly compact models. To address this challenge, we explore quantum computing and introduce Quantum-Gated LiteSSD, a parameter-efficient hybrid quantum--classical detector that reformulates QuCNet-style multi-circuit quantum processing as an identity-centered channel-gating mechanism for spatial feature modulation. Experiments on the Marine Debris Watertank dataset and UATD forward-looking sonar benchmarks demonstrate an effective parameter--accuracy trade-off. The proposed detector achieves 90.84% $\mathrm{mAP}_{50}$ on Watertank with approximately $62\times$ fewer parameters than YOLO26s and $164.3\times$ fewer parameters than SSD-VGG16. On UATD, the model achieves 70.37% $\mathrm{mAP}_{50}$ with only 0.150M parameters, making it approximately $4.1\times$ smaller than SSGA-YOLO while retaining meaningful multi-class detection capability.

abstract: Replication data for a"Nationally Consistent, Locally Incomplete: A Bayesian Remote-Sensing Audit of Rooftop Photovoltaic Registries" (Kasmi et al, 2026, under submission). This repository contains the data that should be unzipped into the `data` folder of the replication code, accessible at https://github.com/gabrielkasmi/pv-registry-audit. Additional resources: Analysis code: https://github.com/gabrielkasmi/pv-registry-audit (this dataset is a supplement to it), Statistical core (Bayesian correction and audit package): http://github.com/gabrielkasmi/bayesian-pv-census/ Detection product: OpenPVMapper v3, deposited at Zenodo at this url : https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21534856 Mapping algorithm: https://github.com/gabrielkasmi/deeppvmapper Annotation tooling: https://github.com/gabrielkasmi/pv-annotation Article preprint : https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16294 Licences 1. Derived from the French transmission system operator's grid-connection registry under an agreement with that operator, subject to disclosure control. 2. French public open data — Licence Ouverte / Open Licence 2.0 (Etalab) data/source/registries/* (RNI extracts, ODRE/data.gouv.fr) data/source/boundaries/communes_simplified.gpkg, departements.geojson, departements_detailed.geojson (IGN ADMIN EXPRESS) 3. Natural Earth — Public domain / CC0data/source/boundaries/world_lowres.geojson — the world basemap, released by Natural Earth under its own no-restrictions terms, not the French open licence. 4. Data produced by the authors — CC BY 4.0data/source/annotations/* (manual annotations), data/source/detections/dpvm_detections_filtered.geojson, data/source/boundaries/dates_patch_communes.csv (manual corrections), and everything under data/intermediate/*.

title: Digitalisation ontology and tool architecture
abstract: This deliverable defines the digitalisation ontology and system architecture of theCOOPERANT-AI TOOL, developed under Subtask 3.5.1. It provides the semantic and digitalfoundations necessary to align the physical and digital development of materials and systems.This work fully aligns with the Data Management Plan (DMP) requirements set out inDeliverable D1.2 under Task 1.2, adhering to the FAIR principles (Findable, Accessible,Interoperable and Reusable) to ensure proper data handling and reproducibility.At the core of this deliverable lies the definition of a graph-based semantic data modeltailored to the project’s specific needs. The COOPERANT ontology serves as the semanticbackbone of the tool, which is outlined in Annexe I: “Visualisation of the ontology inputs”.It is based on linked data principles and standard frameworks like OWL and RDF. Ontologies,modelling standards, and semantic web technologies were examined to identify best practicesand tools for development. The ontology was developed using Protégé and enhanced with theRDFlib and PyVis libraries to incorporate interactive visualisation capabilities. There are threemain parts to the semantic framework of COOPERANT: Inputs, Processing Modules, and Outputs.The framework discusses the semantic annotation and integration of various data sources,such as simulations, experiments, and external databases, enabling the system tocomprehend the data consistently. This semantic foundation is closely tied to the tool'smodular system design and data architecture. It illustrates the significance of ontology infacilitating the integration of various components within a project and work package.

title: Modality-aware differentially private federated learning for partially observed multimodal healthcare prediction
abstract: Multimodal healthcare prediction can benefit from combining structured electronic health records, medical imaging, and acquisition-related metadata, but these modalities are often incompletely observed across patients and unevenly distributed across clinical sites. Federated learning provides a mechanism for collaborative model training without centralizing patient records, yet privacy-preserving federated optimization remains challenging when clients differ in modality availability, update reliability, and data distribution. This study develops MoPA-FL, a modality-aware differentially private federated learning framework for partially observed multimodal healthcare prediction. The framework integrates modality-specific encoders, gated missing-modality fusion, branch-wise differentially private update perturbation, and server-side parameter-group aggregation guided by modality support and update reliability. MoPA-FL was evaluated through controlled federated simulations using the COVID Data for Shared Learning dataset, preserving 4479 structured-record admissions while leveraging an imaging-linked subset of 1859 patients. Under non-IID federated settings, MoPA-FL achieved an AUROC of 0.872 and an AUPRC of 0.683, with higher performance than representative federated, multimodal federated, and privacy-preserving baselines in the evaluated setting. At the configured privacy-budget setting of \(\epsilon =2\) , MoPA-FL achieved an AUROC of 0.847, compared with 0.801 for differentially private federated averaging. These budget values describe the operational accounting configuration; a privacy guarantee for the complete server-observed training transcript remains to be established. These findings suggest that privacy, modality incompleteness, and client heterogeneity should be addressed jointly in multimodal healthcare federated learning.

title: Causal discovery identifies pathways linking physical activity to dementia risk in the UK BioBank
abstract: Physical Activity (PA) is consistently associated with lower risk of dementia, yet the mechanism linking PA to dementia prevention remain incomopletely understood. Here, we integrate large language model (LLM)-guided causal discovery with mediation analysis in 42,293 older adults aged 60 years or older from the UK Biobank to systematically identify pathways connecting objectively measured moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) to dementia risk. Across behavioral, psychological, functional, and clinical domains, causal discovery consistently identified interconnected pathways linking higher MVPA to lower dementia risk through depression, functional capacity, smoking behavior, hypertension, cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, and brain injury. Chain mediation analyses further identified depression as a central pathway, accounting for 15.1% of the overall association between MVPA and dementia risk. Sex-stratified analyses revealed distinct mechanistic patterns, with females exhibiting predominantly metabolic and functional pathways, while males showed behavioral and cardiometabolic cascades involving smoking and cardiovascular disease. Together, these findings suggest that the protective association between PA and dementia is mediated through interconnected behavioral, psychological, and cardiometabolic processes rather than a single pathway. Depression emerged as a prominent and potentially modifiable pathway, highlighting opportunities for integrating dementia prevention strategies that combine PA promotion with mental health and cardiovascular risk management.

title: Positioning manuscripts in the scientific landscape with agentic AI
abstract: Publishing a research manuscript is a routine yet demanding part of scientific life: time-consuming, stressful, and often uncertain in outcome. Recent advances in large language model (LLM)-based agentic AI have shown promise across a range of scientific tasks, and here we ask whether agentic AI can help researchers navigate the publication process itself by reliably inferring a manuscript's eventual publication venue from its content and literature context. We introduce PASS (Publication-oriented Agentic Scientific System), an agentic system that understands manuscripts within their domain-specific literature context and predicts top-matched publication venues. PASS positions each manuscript within its surrounding literature landscape by reconstructing its local scientific neighborhood, tracing its topic trajectory, and reasoning over field-specific journal spaces. Evaluated on a leakage-audited benchmark of over 2,000 preprints across 16 biomedical fields, PASS achieved Top-1 accuracy of 50.3% and Top-5 accuracy of 86.1%, outperforming state-of-the-art LLM baselines and established journal-selection tools. PASS-produced quality scores, such as impact potential and novelty, aligned with independent measures of publication outcome. We also found that the designed literature retrieval module is the strongest performance contributor, particularly for positioning manuscripts relative to nearby work, and that PASS maintained near-full performance from the abstract alone, whereas LLM baselines required the full manuscript text. An independent human evaluation found strong researcher agreement with PASS's manuscript understanding and recommendation rationale. PASS has been released as a public platform (https://ratemypaper.ai/) for broad researcher access.

title: C-MoM: A Multi-Model Collaboration Architecture Organized by Cognitive Function—Preliminary Findings from Its Most Basic Reasoning–Review Collaboration on a Stratified Sample of TruthfulQA
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) still produce hallucinations and factual errors, in part because knowledge and reasoning are entangled inside a single model, so generation and verification lack an independent perspective. Drawing on research on cognitive architectures, this paper presents C-MoM (Cognitive Mixture of Models)—a multi-model collaboration architecture organized around cognitive-function decoupling—and reports a preliminary test of its most basic collaborative unit: reasoning–review collaboration between two independent models. Collaboration is operationalized along two manipulable dimensions—coupling strength (the bandwidth of information exchanged between models) and decision-authority assignment (which party produces the final answer)—and tested on a stratified 305-question sample of TruthfulQA under 11 controlled conditions in 13 runs of deterministic decoding. The results are consistent with an inverted-U relationship between collaboration gains and coupling strength: under-coupling (second pass, self-review) supplies no new information, whereas over-coupling (anchored review, full discussion) undermines independent judgment. Moderately coupled configurations (blind review, feedback–redo) yield non-negative gains in every direction. In particular, blind review adjudicated by the stronger model raises accuracy by 4.9 percentage points over its reasoner's solo baseline (73.4% vs 68.5%; McNemar p = 0.032)—the only statistically significant positive effect across all conditions—while the feedback–redo configuration in which the stronger model serves as reasoner and retains decision authority ties with it for the highest accuracy overall (73.4%), a non-significant 1.9-percentage-point gain over the best single-model baseline (71.5%; p = 0.327). Decision-authority assignment shows a directionally consistent moderating pattern. Error-detection analysis further shows that reviewers are imperfect detectors (sensitivity 58.6%–78.2%) and that self-correction without external information is unreliable and can be harmful (Qwen3 self-review: −15.1 percentage points, the strongest effect observed). Finally, we discuss the ethical risks of consensus errors in such multi-agent systems and offer deployment recommendations for hallucination mitigation.

abstract: Independent maintained research companion for Solver Agent: Towards Emotional and Opponent-Aware Agent for Human-Robot Negotiation. Unavailable historical inputs are explicit. The preferred research citation remains the original paper; software attribution and original source notices are preserved.

title: Reproducibility artifact: fault-injection-guided seccomp profiling for offline-first edge containers
abstract: Reproducibility bundle for the manuscript "Fault-Injection-Guided Seccomp Profiling for Offline-First Edge Containers: Deterministic, Equal-Budget Discovery of Coverage-Gap Syscalls" (submitted to Computers & Security). All artefacts are named in English; documentation is fully bilingual (English documents, Indonesian result reports). Contains all scripts, profiles, raw traces, and results reports needed to regenerate the paper's numbers under the FI-isolated fault-injection methodology: fault taxonomy F1-F8 (event-triggered, seeded), seccomp profiles S_happy*:=S3=86 and S4=92 (with boot- and fold-2 variants), GATE/RQ3 determinism results, RQ2 breakage + CVE gating PoCs, RQ4 performance, RQ5 cross-runtime replication (Go/BEAM/JVM) plus an aarch64 replication. The manuscript itself is NOT included (published separately). See README_ARTEFAK.md and GUIDE_REPRODUCTION.md.

title: Reproduction package: unsupervised and semi-supervised anomaly detection for credit card fraud under chronological evaluation
abstract: Complete reproduction package for the manuscript Rethinking Unsupervised Credit Card Fraud Detection: A Leakage-Controlled Chronological Benchmark (Array, manuscript ARRAY-D-26-04414R1). The notebook benchmarks five classical anomaly detectors (Isolation Forest, Local Outlier Factor, One-Class SVM, DBSCAN, K-Means) on the ULB credit card and PaySim datasets under a chronological protocol. Decision thresholds and score transformations are estimated on a validation window and applied unchanged, so the decision assigned to a transaction does not depend on the other transactions in the evaluation set; this property is verified numerically at run time rather than asserted. The package covers three fitting regimes including a non-deployable oracle reference, a prevalence-controlled comparison of random and chronological splits, rolling-origin evaluation with block-bootstrap intervals, hyperparameter and subsampling sensitivity analyses, a label-efficiency curve for the hybrid bridge, a feature ablation on the synthetic dataset crossed with the ablation of the absolute clocks, and per-transaction operational measurements. Every reported value is traceable to a row of the canonical results file through its run_id. Datasets are not redistributed; both are public and linked in the README. Version 1.2.0 adds notebooks/revision_pipeline_v2_1.ipynb, a corrected pipeline that reproduces the archived results with its default settings, and the results/phase0/ outputs behind the validation-selected hyperparameter configurations, the paired bootstrap comparisons and the per-fold rolling-origin values. Five defects found in a post-revision audit of the code are fixed: a silent fallback in the DBSCAN out-of-sample rule that replaced the core set with the whole reference sample when no core point was found, the absence of any diagnostic for that degeneracy, two mutually inconsistent hyperparameter tie-break rules, an invariance probe that covered only the ensemble, and the absence of the ensemble from the hyperparameter sweep and the operational table. revision_pipeline_v2.ipynb is retained unchanged for provenance. Version 1.3.0 accompanies the second revision. It adds notebooks/revision_R2_reviewer1.ipynb, archived as executed, and its results in results/R2/: a reproduction check of the archived run, five reference-set draws, the four-member ensemble, block-bootstrap intervals with Holm-adjusted paired comparisons, the PaySim temporal analyses without the simulator clock, the ensemble rebuilt from the validation-selected members and the diagnostic of the meta-classifier. It also adds scripts/clock_ablation/, the two cells that ablate the absolute clocks (Time on ULB, step on PaySim) and produce Table 13, with results/canonical_results.csv now holding 8,188 rows, and the script of Figure 1. The hyperparameter selection and results/phase0/ are unchanged from 1.2.0. The saved headline test scores (test_scores.npz, 83 MB) are archived with version 1.2.0 (10.5281/zenodo.22847968).

title: ANALISIS SENTIMEN DAMPAK AI TERHADAP LAPANGAN KERJA DI PLATFORM MEDIA SOSIAL X MENGGUNAKAN ZERO-SHOT LEARNING
abstract: Perkembangan kecerdasan buatan (AI) yang masif memicu perdebatan publik mengenai dampaknya terhadap dunia kerja. Diskusi ini banyak muncul di platform X, menjadikannya sumber data relevan untuk mengkaji persepsi masyarakat. Penelitian ini bertujuan memetakan kecenderungan sentimen masyarakat terhadap dampak AI pada lapangan kerja menggunakan pendekatan Zero-Shot Learning. Sebanyak 384 unggahan dan komentar dikumpulkan dari platform X, melalui preprocessing, kemudian diklasifikasikan ke dalam tiga kategori sentimen positif, negatif, dan netral menggunakan model BART Large MNLI, dengan sebagian data dianotasi manual sebagai acuan evaluasi. Hasil menunjukkan bahwa sentimen positif mendominasi (53,6%), diikuti dengan hasil negatif (40,1%), dan netral (6,2%), mengindikasikan optimisme terhadap manfaat AI meski kekhawatiran atas otomatisasi tetap signifikan. Evaluasi model menghasilkan akurasi 44,74% dan F1-Score tertimbang 0,46, menandakan keterbatasan Zero-Shot Learning dalam menangkap nuansa bahasa Indonesia informal di media sosial. Meski demikian, temuan ini memberikan gambaran awal persepsi publik terhadap AI dan dapat menjadi pertimbangan bagi pemerintah, akademisi, pelaku industri dalam menghadapi transformasi ketenagakerjaan di Indonesia. Kata Kunci: Analisis Sentimen, Artificial Intelligence, Platform Media Sosial X, Zero-Shot Learning, Lapangan Kerja.

title: On the Equivalence of Stochastic Control and Path Space Formulations for Schrödinger Bridges over Compact Connected Lie Groups
abstract: We establish the equivalence between the stochastic optimal control and path space formulations of the Schrödinger bridge problem (SBP) for the kinematic equation on a compact connected Lie group. Using the geometric concepts of horizontal lift and stochastic anti-development, we derive a Girsanov-type change-of-measure result, and show that the expected control energy equals the relative entropy of the controlled path law with respect to the reference Wiener measure. Thus, the SBP is equivalently a path space relative entropy minimization problem subject to prescribed endpoint marginals.Our result has three useful implications. From an analytic viewpoint, the shown equivalence helps prove the existence and uniqueness of the SB. From a probabilistic viewpoint, it helps interpret the SB as the most probable deviation of the uncontrolled stochastic dynamics consistent with the endpoint constraints. From a computational viewpoint, it allows using static Sinkhorn recursions to directly solve the relative entropy minimization problem and compute the optimal path measure. We illustrate the equivalence numerically on the torus $\mathbb{T}^2$. The code is publicly available at: https://github.com/gradslab/LargeDeviationSBP

title: Shot-based variational simulation of the toric code phase transition: Energy, global entanglement, and noise resilience
abstract: We investigate the capability of variational quantum circuits in detecting a topological phase transition within the toric code model subjected to a uniform magnetic field. The detection is carried out via shot-based computations of both the ground state energy and the global entanglement. We begin by employing well-established renormalization techniques to construct a quantum circuit that accurately represents the pure toric code under periodic boundary condition. This circuit is subsequently parameterized to enable a shot-based variational simulation of the ground state in the presence of the magnetic field. Our results demonstrate that even for the minimal lattice sizes and a finite number of measurement shots, the ground state energy exhibits a distinct singularity at the transition point which can be reliably approximated through finite-size scaling analysis. Furthermore, we introduce a secondary variational circuit designed to compute the global entanglement of the generated ground state. We observe that both global entanglement and its conditional counterpart display the expected qualitative behavior at the transition point, consistent with the topological nature of the phase transition. To evaluate the practical viability of our variational approach on real quantum hardware, we systematically examine the detrimental effects of gate noise on the analysis. We find that the topological phase exhibits a notable robustness against noise, manifesting as a linear decrease in the transition point with increasing noise strength.

title: A Prototype of Relational Risk Telemetry for AI-Based Tools and Chatbots
abstract: Conversational systems based on large language models are being deployed as the first line of contact in customer service, yet their quality is still largely measured using process metrics that do not capture phenomena with potential impact on relational outcomes: lack of dialogue progress, failed error-recovery attempts, or silent customer departure without complaint. This paper presents a prototype of a conceptual and implementational framework for conversational risk telemetry, built on two components: an Operational Taxonomy of conversational states and events grounded in service recovery research, and LLM-as-a-Judge, an automated measurement instrument operating on structured rubrics with an evidence-span requirement. The prototype operates in a production environment: 1,069 scored Polish-language customer-service sessions (8,471 messages) under a single pipeline version, with 631 sessions forming the analytical corpus for trajectory-level statistics. In the pilot corpus, only 40% of sessions flagged for priority review close with negative sentiment, supporting the core premise that relational risk is procedural rather than tonal. A judge-model swap experiment on the full corpus quantifies the instrument's model sensitivity (weighted kappa = 0.70 on the priority band, rule-anchored fields effectively invariant at 99.7% agreement). Includes a pre-registered validation plan.

title: Cost-aware adaptive defense against feature-space adversarial attacks in partitioned deep neural networks
abstract: Partitioned deep neural network inference exposes intermediate feature representations to potential manipulation during transmission between computational nodes. Adversarial perturbations injected into these boundary tensors can propagate through the remaining network and cause downstream misclassification, while existing defenses either detect anomalies without restoring prediction reliability or apply unconditional recovery at unnecessary computational cost. This paper presents a cost-aware adaptive defense framework for feature-space adversarial attacks in partitioned deep neural networks operating under realistic communication degradation in distributed edge AI systems. A lightweight detector models clean boundary representations using channel-wise feature statistics and identifies anomalous deviations with controlled false-positive behavior. For flagged samples, a repair module projects anomalous statistics toward the clean region and performs moment-matching correction of the received feature map, with optional masked repair to restrict modification to the most anomalous channels. An MD-gated contextual bandit supervisor then selects the recovery action to balance robustness and computational cost. Experiments on partitioned VGG16 and ResNet50 under channel-sparse Gaussian-noise perturbations, together with an additional iterative query-based feature-space attack based on Natural Evolution Strategies (NES), show that the proposed framework maintains near-clean accuracy, substantially recovers attacked performance, and reduces unnecessary recovery compared with unconditional repair. The results demonstrate that lightweight detection combined with selective and adaptive correction provides an effective defense for robust distributed inference.

title: Not your average podcaster: turn-taking timings and conversational role behavior in AI-generated dialogues
abstract: Abstract What makes artificially generated podcasts feel natural, and what are their current limitations? In this exploratory study, we compare podcasts generated by Google’s NotebookLM Audio Overview feature with naturally produced podcasts to explore two key ingredients of human dialogue, turn-taking timings and contextually appropriate role behavior. Humans excel at predicting where a previous speaker ends their turn, which allows them to chime in with minimal overlap or gap between speaker turns. Humans also follow unwritten rules of conversation to avoid redundancy, provide relevant information, and adhere to socially appropriate behavior within the dynamics of an unfolding conversation. These key ingredients to human conversation pose significant challenges to artificial dialogue generation despite recent advancements in speech recognition, appropriateness of content delivery, and voice production. NotebookLM overcomes some of the traditional pitfalls of spontaneous dialogue generation through avoiding endpoint prediction by including turn-taking and backchanneling in its script writing. It does so by strictly adhering to avoidance of overlaps or gaps. This is unlike what we observe in human podcast dialogues. Where humans show an acute awareness of the changing dynamics between hosts and guests in conversation, and even overlap to show engagement, AI shows little flexibility. We argue that naturalness in dialogue requires a contextually appropriate and addressee-oriented approach to respond to how a conversation unfolds and not just getting the timings right. A novel human intervention feature shows that pre-determining role behavior and turn taking only goes so far in generating natural dialogue: NotebookLM clearly hits its limits when responding to unpredictable intervention. Variable turn-taking timings and adapting conversational role behavior in spontaneous conversation remain unmatched human skills that are indispensable for natural dialogues.

title: VeriDx: Earning the Right to Diagnose with Disease-Centric Verification
abstract: A correct diagnosis can still be reached for the wrong reasons. In clinical reasoning, every disease hypothesis creates obligations: key evidence must be checked, alternatives must be ruled out, contradictions must be resolved, useful tests must be considered, and closure must be justified. Current evaluations of medical LLMs mostly focus on final answers, local steps, or isolated facts, and therefore miss these hypothesis-induced commitments. We introduce \textbf{VeriDx}, a disease-centric verification framework that links free-form diagnostic reasoning to structured disease profiles. VeriDx tracks whether each hypothesis is satisfied, unresolved, or violated its clinical obligations, exposing failures such as missing critical tests, unresolved differentials, ignored contradictions, unsupported claims, and premature closure. We instantiate VeriDx for complex respiratory diagnosis using guideline-derived disease profiles and expert-annotated longitudinal cases. Our results show that many diagnostic errors are not isolated mistakes, but broken commitments made earlier in the reasoning process.

title: Development of Low-Cost Real-Time Driver Drowsiness Detection System using Eye Centre Tracking and Dynamic Thresholding
abstract: One in every five vehicle accidents on the road today is caused simply due to driver fatigue. Fatigue or otherwise drowsiness, significantly reduces the concentration and vigilance of the driver thereby increasing the risk of inherent human error leading to injuries and fatalities. Hence, our primary motive being - to reduce road accidents using a non-intrusive image processing based alert system. In this regard, we have built a system that detects driver drowsiness by real time tracking and monitoring the pattern of the driver's eyes. The stand alone system consists of 3 interconnected components - a processor, a camera and an alarm. After initial facial detection, the eyes are located, extracted and continuously monitored to check whether they are open or closed on the basis of a pixel-by-pixel method. When the eyes are seen to be closed for a certain amount of time, drowsiness is said to be detected and an alarm is issued accordingly to alert the driver and hence, prevent a casualty.

title: Statistical Emergence in Transformer Architectures: A Fuzzy-Enriched Kleisli Category Framework
abstract: We develop a formal theory of statistical emergence in large language models in the [0,1]-enriched Kleisli category Kl(P)_[0,1] of the probability monad on measurable spaces. Layers are Markov kernels carrying graded degrees, the forward pass is Kleisli composition, and a capability is depth-emergent when it is realized by the multi-layer colimit and by no proper sub-part — irreducible to single-layer computation. The sense is narrow: we do not address capabilities appearing discontinuously with scale. We prove two theorems. Every finite transformer chain diagram has a fuzzy colimit with explicitly constructible coherence degree δ_C = ∏_l d_l (Theorem 3.6); and, for a head whose target carries the largest attention mass, entropy uniformly below h forces a worst-case Kleisli degree d_l ≥ e^(−h) (Lemma 4.3), converting an abstract degree condition into a checkable architectural property. We then define a category ComCirc of complete mechanistic circuit descriptions and a map F_K into chain diagrams in Kl(P)_[0,1], and show that induction heads, indirect-object identification (Wang et al., 2022) and greater-than (Hanna et al., 2023) instantiate it, each with a depth-1 impossibility argument. Every coherence degree reported here is measured, not borrowed. On GPT-2 small, over 8 seeds, induction's internal product is δ_C ≈ 0.90 (fifth percentile 0.69), with end-to-end degrees 0.92 for IOI and 0.98 for greater-than. Induction's infimum collapses toward 0 on inputs that make the target ambiguous, instantiating the framework's adversarial-infimum prediction. Whether every complete circuit is depth-emergent under F_K remains an open conjecture (Conjecture 5.9). A self-obscuration bound (Theorem 6.5) limits any depth-k self-assessment of a system's AGI degree by the categorical factor ∏_{l>k} d_l < 1, proved here, times an explicitly assumed self-model-fidelity parameter. This deposit contains two files: the preprint, and a self-contained replication package holding the measurement code, its saved output, the manuscript source, and a determinism receipt recording the SHA-256 of a byte-for-byte verified re-run.

title: TF-IDF and BM25 Are Exact KL Divergences
abstract: TF-IDF and BM25 are two of the most widely used methods for scoring query-document relevance, yet neither has a standard probabilistic derivation that justifies it as a statistical method within a unified framework. We address this gap by showing that both scoring methods admit an exact interpretation as Kullback-Leibler divergences between two probability models. We treat the BM25 variant that includes the plus 1 correction in the IDF term, which is the one used in practice, and also discuss the original BM25 formulation without that correction. The resulting framework provides a common theoretical basis for TF-IDF and BM25, clarifies what they measure, and allows them to be compared theoretically with other information retrieval methods rather than only experimentally.

title: UntitledFederated Privacy-Preserving Feature Selection for University Moral Education Data Using Adaptive Spiral-Flight Sparrow Search Item
abstract: Universities increasingly rely on academic, behavioral, engagement, and student-support records to identify learners who may benefit from timely educational assistance. In multi-institutional settings, however, these records remain distributed across independently governed information systems, while differences in student populations and feature distributions complicate collaborative analysis. This study formulates feature selection in this setting as a horizontal cross-silo problem and proposes an adaptive spiral-flight sparrow search algorithm (ASFL-SSA) within a privacy-preserving federated framework. The framework separates relevance guidance from candidate evaluation. Stage A constructs a global search prior from locally estimated mutual-information scores after clipping and Gaussian perturbation, whereas Stage B evaluates candidate feature masks using securely aggregated client-level validation AUC scores. ASFL-SSA combines prior-guided Tent-chaos initialization, adaptive producer allocation and inertia control, stagnation-triggered spiral exploration, opposition-based search, and budget-aware single-bit refinement. Candidate selection is constrained by a common fitness-evaluation budget, and finalist masks are re-ranked before the selected subset is frozen for downstream modelling. Evaluation follows a three-level design comprising the five-university Institutional Moral-Education Cohort (IMEC) for application-oriented and temporal validation, UCI-697 for reproducible student-risk benchmarking, and Madelon-500 for high-dimensional nonlinear stress testing. Predictive utility is examined together with sparsity, selection stability, cross-client consistency, privacy sensitivity, robustness, computational cost, and communication overhead. The resulting framework provides a compact and auditable approach to federated feature selection while preserving institutional control over student-level records.

title: MorphoNAS-DevPriors: reproducibility companion for 'Grown, not trained: what a developmental map makes likely before selection'
abstract: Code, data, and analysis scripts behind the study of the functional prior that un-evolved MorphoNAS development places on a recurrent network before any learning or selection. The headline is a size/density-controlled Mantel-Haenszel comparison against matched-random wiring, with a paired reward-axis de-confounder showing the enrichment is outcome-dependent. The repository also includes exploratory full-paper material: a cross-family map, an observation-axis de-confounder, a feedback-arc-set recurrence ablation and a structural recurrence measure, a competence-threshold robustness sweep, and structured indirect-encoding (CPPN/HyperNEAT) baselines, whose mechanisms are not yet isolated.

title: ERRE-Sandbox
abstract: A local-LLM multi-agent research apparatus that re-implements the cognitive habits of historical thinkers as agents in a 3D space, in order to study deliberate inefficiency and embodied return. The system separates a deterministic simulation plane (physics, memory geometry, RNG, clocks, identifiers) from a recorded/replayed LLM-invocation plane. This allows byte-identical reproduction of runs across operating systems even though a non-deterministic language model sits inside the loop. Replay consumes committed records, so the byte-parity claim can be verified without running a language model or a GPU.

title: Noah-Parsons/fusion-tree-benchmark: Beating the S+ tree, on real data and against learned indexes
abstract: First complete release: implementation, test suite, measurement harness, and all four experiments. Finding. A correctly implemented fusion tree never beats a cache-conscious B-tree on a 2025 laptop CPU, at any size from 2^8 to 2^25 keys, with either compiler, in either timing mode. At 2^25 keys it costs 579 ns per query against the B-tree's 186 ns (throughput). Its absolute deficit grows with n (18 ns at 2^8, 102 ns at 2^25), so no crossover exists at any input size. Mechanism, measured four ways. Hardware counters: 441 instructions per query against 200, and 730 cycles against 291. Single-node timing: a ~60-cycle dependency chain against ~28 for a vectorised B-tree scan. At identical node size and identical cache-line traffic the fusion tree is still 2.8x slower, so the cause is computation, not memory. Ablations isolate branches, node size and word width. Structural result. The 1993 multiplication sketch does not fit a 64-bit word beyond K = 4 keys per node (0% of random key sets at K = 8), and a 256-bit word only reaches K = 6. The implementations here are viable only because of the PEXT instruction (BMI2, 2013). Scale. 20.5 million correctness checks against brute force and std::lower_bound, zero failures under g++ 16.1 and clang 22.1. 48,600 timings across 10 structures, 3 sessions, 2 compilers, 2 modes, 2 run orders. Limitation. One machine (Intel Core Ultra 7 255HX, Arrow Lake). Static structures only: no insertion or deletion. More machines coming. Full write-up: Experiments_Report_2026-09-10.docx. MIT licensed.

At 2^25 keys it costs 579 ns per query against the B-tree's 186 ns (throughput). Its absolute deficit grows with n (18 ns at 2^8, 102 ns at 2^25), so no crossover exists at any input size. Mechanism, measured four ways. Hardware counters: 441 instructions per query against 200, and 730 cycles against 291. Single-node timing: a ~60-cycle dependency chain against ~28 for a vectorised B-tree scan. At identical node size and identical cache-line traffic the fusion tree is still 2.8x slower, so the cause is computation, not memory. Ablations isolate branches, node size and word width. Structural result. The 1993 multiplication sketch does not fit a 64-bit word beyond K = 4 keys per node (0% of random key sets at K = 8), and a 256-bit word only reaches K = 6. The implementations here are viable only because of the PEXT instruction (BMI2, 2013). Scale. 20.5 million correctness checks against brute force and std::lower_bound, zero failures under g++ 16.1 and clang 22.1. 48,600 timings across 10 structures, 3 sessions, 2 compilers, 2 modes, 2 run orders. Limitation. One machine (Intel Core Ultra 7 255HX, Arrow Lake). Static structures only: no insertion or deletion. More machines coming. Full write-up: Experiments_Report_2026-09-10.docx. MIT licensed.

title: Schizophrenia Detection from EEG Signals: A Transformer Framework with Spectrogram Representation
abstract: Schizophrenia is a serious psychiatric disorder that affects millions of people worldwide, and its diagnosis remains primarily dependent on clinical assessment. Electroencephalography (EEG) provides a non-invasive approach to investigate brain activity and has shown potential to support automated Schizophrenia detection. However, existing EEG-based classification studies often suffer from limitations including small datasets, inconsistent preprocessing strategies, and evaluation protocols that may not adequately prevent subject-related data leakage. In this study, we propose an EEG-based Schizophrenia classification framework that transforms preprocessed EEG recordings into time-frequency representations using the Short-Time Fourier Transform. The generated spectrogram images are classified using both conventional Machine Learning algorithms, including Support Vector Machines, Random Forests, and XGBoost, and Deep Learning models, including convolutional architectures and CNN-Transformer hybrids. To ensure reliable evaluation, all data partitions are performed at the subject level, and image-level predictions are aggregated into subject-level decisions. On the independent test set of 18 subjects, the CNN-Transformer (CT-SZ) model achieves a subject-level AUC-ROC of 95.00%, while the CNN + Squeeze-and-Excitation + Transformer (CST-SZ) model achieves 92.50%.
